title: NeoHaskell homepage
question: Choose the homepage direction. Each keeps the original logo and leads into installation and agent setup.

options.label: Logic pieces
options.thesis: An application takes shape from a few understandable rules.
options.viewport: One continuous geometric composition carries the offer, a seat-reservation example, and the start of the setup guide.
options.risk: Playful geometry must explain real behavior without making setup feel like a puzzle.

raised.raise: Each visible result traces back to the request and rule that produced it.
One coherent visual field carries the whole example, rather than decorative pieces.
Motion has one clear before-and-after beat, with a complete still state.
The opening stays simple; precise setup detail appears only at the next reading level.

options.label: Assembly guide
options.thesis: Make the route from an idea to a working application legible at a glance.
options.viewport: An oversized open instruction sheet links an app idea to rules, events, and the first setup step.
options.risk: The most immediately familiar option; instructional design needs enough character to be memorable.

options.label: Rules in view
options.lineage: Darkroom exposure records and translucent tracing sheets
options.thesis: Reveal the rules and accepted history underneath an application’s visible state.
options.viewport: Overlapping readable layers carry request, rule, and event; a clear opening in the sheet carries Start building.
options.case: Product clarity holds through visible layers; the unfamiliar photographic metaphor weakens audience identification.
options.risk: Dense labels and translucent layers could make a beginner’s first encounter feel technical.

options.label: Every change in frame
options.lineage: Film cutting benches and indexed frame strips
options.thesis: See an application’s history as a sequence you can inspect one event at a time.
options.viewport: One spanning event strip carries the sample behavior; the offer and setup entry are readable parts of that strip.
options.case: Product clarity holds through the event sequence; film-editing language is less familiar to application builders.
options.risk: It can suggest a video product unless NeoHaskell and the application example lead every frame.

options.label: Instruction weave
options.thesis: Individual instructions form an application whose result can be traced.
options.viewport: An instruction band feeds a woven behavior pattern with a setup link in the readable band.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and product clarity: weaving and binary cards introduce two unfamiliar translations.
options.kept: Trace a visible result back to the exact request and rule.
options.risk: Suggests low-level binary programming rather than easy application building.

options.label: Rules of the garden
options.thesis: Different rules produce different observable paths.
options.viewport: One illustrated field exposes an example rule alongside the setup action.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and product clarity: rain laws obscure what the language and framework actually do.
options.kept: Commit to one coherent visual environment.
options.risk: Could read as an art experiment or physics simulator.

options.label: Cause and effect
options.thesis: A clear action produces a visible consequence.
options.viewport: One rounded scene shows the example change and an unmistakable setup action.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and product clarity: comic motion attracts attention without explaining the framework.
options.kept: Give the example a single readable before-and-after beat.
options.risk: The character animation can overshadow the language.

options.label: The setup sleeve
options.thesis: A concise product promise opens into precise setup instructions.
options.viewport: One simple face carries the offer while a dense wrapping band exposes installation steps.
options.case: Loses on audience identification and product clarity: specialist sleeve references and crowded credits add reading effort.
options.kept: Separate the simple opening promise from precise setup details.
options.risk: A visitor may see packaging before understanding the product.

canonCard.label: Familiar developer homepage
canonCard.thesis: A polished, conventional language homepage with a direct setup path.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar headline and introduction lead into a setup button, product example, and concise benefits.
canonCard.risk: Easy to recognize as a developer product, with less distinctive identity.
